title: Pacifico matches the open-source-sovereignty thesis exactly at four-person scale
content:
Pacifico ships its own open-source framework, racletteJS, states an 'Open Source First' position, and holds OSBA and digital-sovereignty memberships. The research describes the ideological match as exact: the firm has already made the commitments the thesis assumes, so none of them has to be argued for.

The counterweight is size — a four-person shop. Both facts sit in the same sentence of the research deliberately, because ideological alignment and delivery capacity are separate axes and this lead scores at opposite ends of them. Neither fact cancels the other out; they decide different things.

In practice alignment decides whether a conversation is worth starting, and capacity decides what may be asked of it. A four-person shop that owns its framework can co-build a reference quickly, precisely because it controls its own code and has no committee to convince, and it cannot absorb volume. Recording both prevents the lead from being over-ranked on enthusiasm or dismissed on headcount.
